title: County EM Call: Oil in the Ditch at Mill Ridge Ramp

transcript.speaker: Ironbark Emergency Line
transcript.text: Ironbark Pipeline emergency line. I'm patching you through to the on-call Qualified Individual now. Please hold.

transcript.speaker: County EM
transcript.text: Morning. This is Dana Whitlock, duty officer at Prairie Bend County Emergency Management. Our 911 just took a call from a fisherman at the Mill Ridge boat ramp. He says there's black oil running in the ditch by the river, and it stinks like rotten eggs. Is that your pipeline?

transcript.speaker: County EM
transcript.text: Okay. Well, nobody from Ironbark has called us. Not one call. I found out from 911. How much are we talking about, and when did it start?

transcript.speaker: County EM
transcript.text: I need one number I can give the commissioners and the sheriff. I don't want three different numbers going around by lunchtime.

transcript.speaker: County EM
transcript.text: That rotten egg smell. Is that dangerous? The fisherman's still standing right there, and the sheriff has a deputy on the way to the ramp. Do I keep people back? How far?

transcript.speaker: County EM
transcript.text: Just so you know, I put it out on our partner page at 06:39. It says unconfirmed crude oil in a drainage ditch near the Mill Ridge ramp on the Kansas River, source possibly a pipeline, updates to follow. That goes to the spill cooperative's duty phone and the Sterling Bluff water plant, among others.

transcript.speaker: County EM
transcript.text: Hang on. Hang on, 911 has him back on the other line. Okay. He says it's in the river now. A brown sheen, moving downstream fast. That was 06:41.

transcript.speaker: County EM
transcript.text: Who's calling the water plants? Prairie Bend Rural Water's intake is only eleven miles down from there. And Sterling Bluff after that. Are you calling them, or am I?

transcript.speaker: County EM
transcript.text: Alright. Give me a callback number and a name for your liaison. I'll be in our EOC. I need an update from you within the hour, not from 911.

voiceStyles.Ironbark Emergency Line: Calm answering-service operator, brisk and neutral
voiceStyles.County EM: Woman in her 40s, county duty officer, clipped and irritated at first, then urgent when the second 911 call comes in; radio chatter faintly behind her

instructorNote: This inject tests whether the QI confirms the release to the county using the agreed 2,700–3,500 bbl range (planning figure 3,100 bbl), logs the call as the county notification, warns the county to keep people away from the ditch because of H2S, and then makes the remaining SNIMTA 2 calls in order. Watch for these responses: ENVL takes 06:40/06:41 river entry as the trajectory start. OSRO alerts crews but waits for QI activation. SBWD logs the unofficial page under Sterling Bluff plan step 1 and starts hourly intake sampling. If the QI is asked for a cause, they should not guess one.
